insider_note: xeˣ is a product, and its derivative by the product rule is exactly eˣ(1+x) — the whole numerator here IS the derivative of the argument inside cos², which is the signal to substitute the argument whole.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Substitute t = xeˣ
steps.why: By the product rule, d/dx(xeˣ) = xeˣ+eˣ = eˣ(x+1), which is exactly the numerator — so the whole numerator dx converts to dt, leaving a plain sec²t to integrate.
common_mistakes: Missing the product rule when differentiating xeˣ, and instead treating eˣ and x as needing separate substitutions.
Writing 1/cos²t as cos²t instead of sec²t.
steps.memory_tip: d/dx(xeˣ) = eˣ(1+x) by the product rule — the exact numerator here, which is why t=xeˣ is the substitution to spot.

steps.label: Integrate and back-substitute for the final answer
steps.why: ∫sec²t dt = tant + c is a standard derivative, and substituting t=xeˣ back in gives the final answer as a tangent of the product xeˣ.
common_mistakes: Writing sin(xeˣ) or cos(xeˣ) instead of tan(xeˣ) — ∫sec²t dt is specifically tant, no other trig function.
Forgetting to substitute xeˣ back in for t.
steps.memory_tip: ∫sec²t dt = tant — one of the six basic trig derivatives, worth having instantly available.
